title: Complaint about a tuba-playing leader who controls the money
summary: Guesnon says phonies who control the money get into the spotlight and cannot be pushed out, using a tuba player as the example.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: It's pretty fair, I mean. Yeah? I mean, it's not the George Lewis record. No, no, no, no. I can't see why he should be there with us. Well, I mean, you know, he's cutting in on everything. Like, I'm telling you, why hire a tuba player and pay him two, three, four hundred dollars, when I can come into the tuba playing?
I think he is the kind that wants to be on a picture with the band. Oh, he wants everything, yeah.

And raise advertisements. Yeah, that's what I'm saying. These kind of people, them phonies, you see? But, you know what I mean? As long as they're controlling the money, you can't tell them they're a phony. No. They're going to be in the spotlight of everything with you. You can't tell them nothing because they're controlling the money. See, that's psychology, you see what I mean? If the guy was broke, you could put him out. Yeah. You can't put him out because he becomes the boss. Yeah. Now, whether I'm good or not, I'll come sit behind you and play, I'll play it and then he gets to this tuba player, let me see how you make that. Get to the other one, let me see how you do that. He listens, he begs, he borrow, he... And that's the way it is now. I mean, he didn't join the union and everything. He's a full-fledged union musician. Isn't he in the union?
